subject: MedSpire retention exception — exec approval path and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@medspire.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed path: MedSpire retention options and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and what I think makes the most sense based on your privacy team constraints:

- Current ask: MedSpire needs a shorten/limited retention window for KV/prefix caches and logs (PII removed at ingestion), ideally as close to 0 days as possible for clinical queries.
- Our risk/ops trade: 0-retention (no KV persist) prevents user-specific caching and harms latency for long multiprompt sessions; a very short window (1–7 days) preserves some performance while meeting most audit requirements.
- Evidence items you requested: SOC 2 evidence, log redaction flow, and a write-up on our ephemeral handling options.

Proposed starting point (what Redwood can offer now):
1) 7-day KV/log retention with automated PII redaction at ingestion (we can scope additional redaction rules).
2) Option to enable a zero-persist pilot for a subset of routes (no KV persisted to disk; cache only in-memory per-request) for high-risk endpoints.
3) Signed operational controls addendum (short-form) + audit snapshot export for your legal team.

Next steps I recommend:
- Elena: confirm whether MedSpire requires 0-persist for all clinical routes or just a subset (triage 2–3 endpoints).
- I will pull together the playbook excerpt and a proposed one-page concession we can take to our legal/ops for exec approval. Attached is a draft playbook and a simple exceptions table for you to review.

If it helps, I can also escalate a specific exec approval route (sales + security + legal signoff) to move a 7-day pilot faster.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: SaaS_Data_Retention_Playbook_v2.pdf (summary), retention_exceptions_table.xlsx (editable)

From: Elena Voss <elena.voss@medspire.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Murphy <john.murphy@medspire.com>, legal@medspire.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed path: MedSpire retention options and next steps

Olga — appreciate the clear summary. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) Scope: we need 0-persist for all endpoints that process PHI or clinician notes. That is our preference. If a complete 0-persist rollout is not feasible immediately, we will accept a timeboxed pilot but will need a clear rollback/fallback policy.
2) Evidence: please provide SOC2 Type II report redacted for vendor distribution, and a technical note that explains how your redaction pipeline works (where PII is removed, how long raw input is stored before redaction).
3) Legal: our GC wants an exceptions playbook that commits to retention windows and an agreed-to notification period for any incident impacting ephemeral stores.

Can you put together the one-page concession and mark which items need executive signoff vs. operational acceptance? Happy to review and route to our legal/security.

— Elena
Elena Voss
Privacy Lead, MedSpire Health
elena.voss@medspire.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@medspire.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed path: MedSpire retention options and next steps

Elena — thanks, that's super helpful. Quick responses inline: 

1) Scope: Understood that PHI/clinician notes require 0-persist. We can propose a two-track approach:
   - Track A (fast): a 7-day KV/log retention pilot for non-PHI routes to preserve perf while legal completes review.
   - Track B (target): 0-persist for PHI routes implemented as an opt-in flag; we can enable a zero-persist execution path that keeps only in-memory ephemeral caches (no disk writes) for the flagged routes. We can commit to scheduling a pilot of Track B within 30 days of acceptance.
2) Evidence: Attached SOC2 redacted summary and a technical note describing redaction stages. The Playbook doc includes the redaction flow; see section 2.2.
3) Legal: We'll produce a one-page concession that distinguishes operational concessions vs. exec-level waivers (we'll flag the items that require exec approval).

Next steps: I will (1) update the attached one-page concession (proposal_medspire_7day-kv.docx), (2) route to our security ops for a written fallback policy, and (3) request an expedited review from Sales leadership for exec approval on the 0-persist pilot.

If you can identify 2–3 endpoints for Track B (PHI), we'll map them to our network/routing flags and provide an implementation ETA.

Olga

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MedSpire retention — suggested exec language and next steps

Olga — looped in Aditya for leadership approval. Suggested language for the one-pager that will make it easier for our legal and security to sign off:

- Proposal summary (one line): Redwood to support a timeboxed 7-day retention pilot for non-PHI routes and enable a zero-persist execution path for PHI routes subject to security validation and exec approval.
- Exec ask: authorize a single 30-day zero-persist pilot for up to 3 flagged endpoints; authority requested: Sales Director + Head of Security + General Counsel.
- Operational safeguards: PII redaction at ingestion, ephemeral-only in-memory caches for zero-persist routes, incident notification within 48 hours for any data-store exposure.
- Rollback: automatic reversion to 7-day retention for affected routes if the pilot uncovers data integrity or availability issues.

I also included a short set of suggested handoff notes for Security Ops to implement the in-memory flags. If you want, I can draft the one-pager and have Legal circle back with redlines.

— Marissa
Director, Sales Operations

To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@medspire.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: MedSpire retention exception — one-pager and exec path (for your review)

Elena — attaching the requested one-pager (attached) that separates operational concessions from items requiring exec approval. Summary below: 

- Fast path (operational): 7-day retention for non-PHI routes; PII redaction at ingestion; SOC2 summary attached; Security Ops to provide fallback policy. No exec signoff required.
- Exec path (required for PHI zero-persist): Single 30-day zero-persist pilot for up to 3 flagged endpoints. Approval required from Redwood Sales Director + Redwood Head of Security + Redwood GC. We will provide a weekly status summary and automatic rollback triggers.

Please confirm whether MedSpire can identify the 2–3 PHI endpoints for Track B and whether MedSpire legal would accept the 48-hour incident notification window. Once you confirm, I'll request exec signoff and share the final concession with your GC.

Thanks and speak soon —
Olga
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal_medspire_7day-kv.docx (one-pager)
